title: The human musculoskeletal network: a muscle's structural impact corresponds to its cortical motor map

dataset.name: Human musculoskeletal hypergraph (Murphy et al. 2018)
dataset.version: PhysioMSKNet bundled data digitised from Murphy et al. 2018, PLoS Biology
dataset.record: the whole-body muscle-bone hypergraph -- 173 bones (vertices) and 270 muscles (hyperedges) -- with the paper's cortical motor-homunculus correspondence and muscle-recovery data
dataset.citation: Murphy AC, Muldoon SF, Baker D, Lastowka A, Bennett B, Yang M, Bassett DS. Structure, function, and control of the human musculoskeletal network. PLoS Biology 2018;16(1):e2002811 (CC-BY 4.0). Data bundled in PhysioMSKNet.

proposition: The body is a network: bones are nodes and muscles are hyperedges spanning the bones they attach to. Building this whole-body muscle-bone hypergraph with the ecosystem recovers the structure Murphy et al. (2018) described -- 173 bones and 270 muscles -- and reproduces its central neuro-anatomical finding: a muscle's structural IMPACT (how much removing it perturbs the network) corresponds to its representation in the cortical motor HOMUNCULUS. Regressing impact against the homunculus map gives R^2 = 0.517 (F = 20.4, p = 2.4e-4 over 21 body regions), matching the paper's R^2 = 0.52 (F = 21.3) -- the somatotopic motor map mirrors the mechanical network. The muscles the brain devotes the most cortex to are the ones whose removal most perturbs the skeleton.

claims.statement: R-squared of the impact-vs-cortical-homunculus regression (matching the paper's 0.52)
body regions in the homunculus correspondence

validation.reference: Murphy et al. (2018, PLoS Biology) modelled the human body as a muscle-bone hypergraph (bones = nodes, muscles = hyperedges) and showed its central result: a muscle's structural impact on the network corresponds to its cortical motor representation (homunculus), R^2 = 0.52. A correct implementation must (1) build the hypergraph at the paper's scale (173 bones, 270 muscles), and (2) reproduce the impact-homunculus correspondence -- which the ecosystem does at R^2 = 0.517 (F = 20.4, p = 2.4e-4 over 21 regions), matching the paper.
validation.data: REAL -- Murphy et al. 2018 (PLoS Biology, CC-BY 4.0), the whole-body muscle-bone hypergraph + the paper's homunculus and recovery data, bundled in PhysioMSKNet
validation.note: The reproducible finding is the impact-vs-homunculus correspondence (R^2 = 0.517 vs the paper's 0.52; F = 20.4 vs 21.3), on the paper-scale hypergraph (173 bones, 270 muscles). HONEST scope: (1) the data are the paper's own (digitised figures + the MSK model), so this validates the ecosystem's hypergraph construction + network/regression machinery against the published result, not an independent cohort; (2) the impact-vs-RECOVERY clinical model (paper Fig 3b) reproduces the significant, positive direction (F = 8.3, p = 0.014) but a LOWER R^2 (0.41 vs the paper's 0.76) -- the paper's recovery model used additional structure/weighting not fully captured here; reported, not hidden; (3) the homunculus correspondence is over 21 aggregated body regions.

open_questions.q: Fully reproducing the impact-vs-recovery model to the paper's R^2 = 0.76 (its exact covariate set and weighting), and driving the hypergraph with subject-specific EMG (emgDrivenJointMoment / muscle-synergy networks) rather than the reference anatomy, would extend this from a structural reproduction to a personalised musculoskeletal-network analysis. Documented, not escalated.
